monthly_review.summary: This month shows a sharp drop in volume and frequency but notable intensity shifts — pace improved while HR rose, suggesting reduced aerobic efficiency at higher effort. The runner is trading endurance stimulus for more zone 3–4 work.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 3–4 time jumped from 22% to 44% of total HR distribution this month — nearly double last month’s combined volume in threshold and hard zones.

goal_tracker.message: You need 33.4 more km across 6 sessions in the remaining 26 days — averaging 5.6 km per session — to match last month’s distance. At your current pace of ~8:46 min/km, that’s ~50 minutes per run.

insights.title: Efficiency dip despite faster pace
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency fell from 13.42 to 13.31 km/hr per bpm, even though avg pace improved by 25 sec/km — indicating less physiological economy at higher intensities, likely due to disproportionate zone 3–4 work (44% vs 22% last month) without sufficient Z2 foundation.

insights.title: Overreliance on threshold and hard efforts
insights.body: Z3+Z4 now accounts for 44% of HR time (22% each), up from 22% last month (19% Z3 + 3% Z4), while Z1+Z2 dropped from 79% to 49%. This suggests under-recovery and potential fatigue accumulation.

insights.title: Cadence-stride trade-off evident
insights.body: Cadence increased +3 spm (146 → 149) but stride length dropped significantly in the 10.0 km run (72.5 cm) vs shorter runs (e.g., 94.7 cm at 7:03 min/km), indicating inefficient form breakdown at endurance pace — possibly due to accumulated fatigue or insufficient Z2 volume.

insights.title: Low training consistency with high variability
insights.body: Four runs in June include three on the same day (June 4: 0.5 km, 1.0 km, 1.0 km), all with widely divergent paces (7:03–9:32 min/km) and HR (136–159 bpm), suggesting unstructured recovery or misaligned session intent — undermining aerobic development.

recommendations.action: Do one 6.0 km Zone 2 run at avg HR ≤135 bpm (target pace ~8:50–9:20 min/km) before June 15
recommendations.reason: Your Z2 % dropped from 43% to 36% and avg HR rose +9 bpm — this rebuilds aerobic base and lowers HR drift at sub-threshold pace.

recommendations.action: Replace one upcoming run with a 20-min easy jog (HR ≤130 bpm, no pace target) focused solely on cadence rhythm (146–148 spm) and ground contact <315 ms
recommendations.reason: Recent runs show elevated ground contact (320–330 ms) during slow efforts and vertical oscillation spikes (9.2 cm) at faster paces — reinforcing neuromuscular efficiency at low load is needed.

recommendations.action: Skip any run if morning resting HR is ≥8 bpm above your 7-day average (track via Garmin), and substitute with 15 min dynamic mobility + breathing drill
recommendations.reason: Aerobic TE dropped from 2.7 to 2.2 and Z1 time fell sharply — early HR elevation is a sensitive marker of incomplete recovery; this prevents compounding fatigue.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish autonomic control and metabolic efficiency through consistent low-intensity stimulus, emphasizing HR discipline, rhythmic cadence, and recovery awareness — not speed or distance.
